components.description: BarChart compares amounts across a few categories: orders by weekday, sales by quarter. It takes rows and the names of the fields to draw, so the same rows can feed another chart or a table. Each category can be pressed to read its value, several series stand side by side, and values below zero hang from the same line.

notes: Each category is read as its name and values: "Thu: 163", or "Q3: Online $55k, In store $33k". With `onSelect` each is a button that reports pressed; without it the plot is a list.
With `summarize`, a sentence with the range, the lowest and highest values and the trend is read before the bars.

Choosing a category is reported as pressed on its button. Where the bars carry no figures (grouped bars, more than eight bars) a readout line above the plot shows the chosen category and announces it; where every bar carries its value there is no readout line.
Figures over the bars and the scale label are hidden from assistive tech: each category already reads its values.
The chosen category keeps its colour and the others step back to 30%, which is not a contrast claim: the pressed state and the readout say which is chosen.

A category's press target is its full-height slot, as wide as the plot divided by the number of categories: 41 px for seven bars at 360 pt, under 10 px for thirty. Past 36 categories the bars are not buttons.
The zero line is a quiet rule with no contrast minimum: the bars' own feet show where zero is.
A chart is one element per category and about a dozen more, whatever the number of bars; the bars themselves are two to four drawings.
Series in a group differ by colour and by position, and the legend lists them in the order drawn.

components.description: Chart is what BarChart, LineChart and PieChart share, and the frame for a plot of your own. It gives the plot a fixed height, names the chart for assistive tech, reads a summary sentence, and swaps the plot for a skeleton, a message or an error. ChartLegend and ChartReadout, from the same import, are the legend and the line that shows the chosen datum.

notes: A group named by `label`, read in order: the title when it differs from the name, the description, the summary, the readout, the marks, the legend.
The readout is a status region: choosing a datum announces its category and figures.

components.description: Stat shows a number a person checks often: revenue, open orders, a response time.
